briefing.body: On 2 November Iran said a Qatar-brokered plan could reopen Hormuz within two days if the US meets its demands, including lifting its naval blockade. Washington says it is in no rush. The strait is still closed to shipping, with 151 ships holding position on 3 November. Brent closed at $104.77 on 2 November, down 7.6%. OPEC+ kept December output unchanged.
briefing.short: Iran says Hormuz could reopen within two days if its terms are met. Brent fell 7.6% to $104.77 on 2 November.
briefing.title: Hormuz offer sends Brent down to $105

briefing.body: Xeneta puts Far East to North Europe at $3,698/FEU (+6.8% week on week) and the Mediterranean at $4,442 on 23 October. Drewry's index has Shanghai–Rotterdam at $3,686 (+1%) and Shanghai–Genoa flat at $4,151 on 29 October. Carriers blank 56 of 714 east–west sailings in weeks 44 to 48 and raise rates again on 1 November.
briefing.short: Xeneta has Asia to North Europe at $3,698/FEU. Drewry's Shanghai–Rotterdam rose another 1% to $3,686 on 29 October.
briefing.title: Asia–Europe freight rises again

briefing.body: Beijing suspended its October 2025 export controls on rare earths, battery materials and graphite anodes until 10 Nov 2026 (Announcement No. 70). On 28 September MOFCOM extended the US–China trade truce to 10 Jan 2027, without naming the rare earth pause, and no notice has moved its date since. Licences for seven heavy rare earths stay in force. Chinese magnet exports fell 6.1% to 5,774 t in September.
briefing.short: The pause on controls for rare earths runs out in a week, on 10 November. No notice has moved the date.
briefing.title: Pause on Chinese export controls ends on 10 November

briefing.body: Alphaliner counts 24 of 46 direct Far East–Europe services in the Red Sea: 63% of capacity, 70% to the Mediterranean and 58% to North Europe. Maersk aims for a full return by March 2027. Sea-Intelligence puts September schedule reliability at 50.6%, near a four-year low, as networks shift. Freightos expects a full return in Q1 2027.
briefing.short: Alphaliner: 63% of Far East–Europe capacity is back in the Red Sea, 58% to North Europe. Full return expected by Q1.
briefing.title: Nearly two thirds of Asia–Europe capacity back in Suez

briefing.body: The 9 October deal eases licences for rare earths and magnets and caps Chinese hybrid car exports to the EU at 350,000 a year for four years. EU leaders have backed an instrument that could limit China's access to the single market; batteries are expected among the first targets. Von der Leyen plans proposals in December on dependence on single suppliers. Political talks follow in January and March 2027.
briefing.short: The hybrid deal caps Chinese hybrid cars at 350,000 a year. Leaders back a tool to limit China's access to the EU market.
briefing.title: EU and China: deals, and a tougher line

briefing.body: In the week to 27 October ships waited 1.36 days at Rotterdam, 1.31 at Antwerp, 1.11 at Hamburg and 1.09 at Bremerhaven, where yards are at 90%. Rotterdam closed for high winds on 23–25 October and barge and feeder delays run 12–72 hours. Italy registered a 24-hour port strike for 30 October. German port wages are settled for a year.
briefing.short: Ships wait over a day at Rotterdam, Antwerp and Hamburg. Rotterdam closed for wind on 23–25 October.
briefing.title: Rotterdam, Antwerp and Hamburg congested

briefing.body: ACEA counted 290,117 battery-electric cars in the EU in September, up 72.9% and a 29.9% share. From January to September there were 1,931,465 (+48.5%), 22.7% of the market against 16.1% a year ago. Germany registered 88,599 in September, a record 34.5% share. Every one of them comes out of warranty a few years from now.
briefing.short: In September 29.9% of new cars in the EU were electric, 72.9% more than a year ago. This year so far the share is 22.7%.
briefing.title: Electric cars take 30% of EU sales in September

briefing.body: DDR4 8Gb contract prices averaged a record $27.50 in October, up 5.77% on September, while MLC NAND was flat at $30.61 (DRAMeXchange). TrendForce expects conventional DRAM up 10–15% in Q4, and Micron says 2027 and 2028 will be tighter still. Control boards in inverters and onboard chargers cost more.
briefing.short: Memory chip prices keep rising: TrendForce expects DRAM contracts up 10–15% in Q4. Micron sees 2027 and 2028 even tighter.
briefing.title: Memory crunch hits electronics

briefing.body: Standard LFP prismatic cells from China cost $57.37/kWh in September, 5.1% less than in August, and NCM cells fell 6.8% over the quarter (Benchmark). Lithium prices dropped sharply on 16 September. Cheaper cells mean cheaper battery modules: the stock you hold is worth a little less.
briefing.short: LFP cells from China at $57/kWh in September. Lithium fell sharply in mid-September.
briefing.title: Battery cells get cheaper again

briefing.body: The global Baltic Air Freight Index rose 4.7% in the seven days to 19 October and is 26.4% higher than a year ago. Rates out of Hong Kong and Shanghai have also been rising. Jet fuel is up 113.7% year on year. The week before, after Golden Week, the index had slipped 2.1%.
briefing.short: The Baltic Air Freight Index rose 4.7% in the week to 19 October and is 26% above last year. Jet fuel has doubled.

src.name: TAC Index via Air Cargo News

briefing.title: Air freight rates climb again

briefing.body: The Commission confirms the battery passport becomes mandatory on 18 February 2027 for EV, light transport, home storage and industrial batteries. It updated the list of data points on 19 October 2026. Each module must carry its origin, materials and carbon footprint, which helps workshops judge used and repaired packs.
briefing.short: From 18 February 2027 every EV battery placed on the EU market needs a digital passport.
briefing.title: Battery passport due on 18 February 2027

briefing.body: Poland is pursuing rail operators, forwarders and customs agents for duties and VAT on imports through Małaszewicze from 2021 to 2026 that an EU probe found fraudulent. On 20 October Kazakhstan and Azerbaijan signed an agreement to standardise Middle Corridor operations; China–Europe container transit on the corridor rose 64% in January to September.
briefing.short: Poland is billing rail and customs firms for duties on fraudulent imports via Małaszewicze. The Middle Corridor gets common rules.
briefing.title: China–EU rail: Małaszewicze customs claims, new corridor

outcomes.body: China’s Ministry of Commerce extends the suspension of the controls until November 2027. The market breathes a sigh of relief.
outcomes.title: Beijing extends the pause by a year

outcomes.body: China brings back export licences for permanent magnets and some batteries. Clearance takes weeks, and prices rise across the industry.
outcomes.title: Licences return for magnets and batteries

outcomes.body: Beijing brings back every measure from October 2025. Exports of batteries and of compressors with magnets need licences, and factories cut production for export.
outcomes.title: Chinese export controls return in full

preview.body: The pause on export controls runs out on 10 November. After the 9 October agreements Brussels hopes for an extension, but analysts do not rule out a return of licensing for magnets and batteries. Your battery modules, heat pumps and drive units come mainly from China.

choices.desc: Extra orders for battery modules and thermal parts in China, expedited (+3% on price).
choices.label: Build 4 weeks of stock

choices.desc: Urgent audit: €220k and 12 days instead of 28. Hanbit makes battery modules and heat pumps.
choices.label: Fast-track Hanbit (Korea)

choices.desc: No extra cost. You stick with the current plan.
choices.label: Wait for the decision

preview.title: In a week: Beijing decides on export controls

outcomes.body: Iran and the US reach a deal, and tankers start leaving the Persian Gulf. Oil gets cheaper and carriers cut their bunker surcharges.
outcomes.title: Strait of Hormuz reopens

outcomes.body: Talks collapse, and there are incidents with tankers in the Gulf of Oman. Brent goes up, and bunker surcharges with it.
outcomes.title: Escalation around Hormuz

events.body: The last big carriers, Evergreen and Zim among them, restore their schedules through the Red Sea. Return legs stop going round the Cape, and the freed-up fleet pushes rates down.
events.title: Suez return completes

outcomes.body: Ministers confirm the easier licensing for rare earths and magnets. The Commission puts new trade defence measures on hold.
outcomes.title: EU and China confirm the agreements

outcomes.body: Brussels finds the progress insufficient and opens an anti-subsidy investigation into parts for electric cars. Provisional duties are possible in about four months.
outcomes.title: Commission probes subsidies for Chinese car batteries and power electronics

events.body: The Commission imposes provisional countervailing duties: 18% on power electronics and 15% on battery modules from China. Goods already in transit pay the duty on import. Competitors raise their prices.
events.title: Provisional duties on Chinese car batteries and power electronics

events.body: Following the American rules on connected cars, the government limits remote access by makers from outside the EU to the electronics in cars on Polish roads. Some fleet customers now want power electronics and batteries made outside China.
events.title: Poland limits remote access to car electronics

outcomes.body: Germany adds a battery health check to the two-yearly car inspection. Owners bring in the cars that fail, and workshops order battery modules.
outcomes.title: The inspection tests every electric car’s battery

outcomes.body: A dispute over the test method delays the new check. Owners put off battery repairs until the rules are clear.
outcomes.title: The battery check is delayed

events.title: Battery checks at the car inspection

outcomes.body: Every new battery module needs a passport. Some Chinese suppliers are not ready, and shipments wait for paperwork.
outcomes.title: Passports start on time

outcomes.body: The Commission gives importers six more months for stock already in Europe. Business carries on as before.
outcomes.title: Brussels allows a grace period

events.body: Beijing closes small lithium mines in Jiangxi over their permits. Lithium and cell prices rise for a second month in a row, and battery modules in warehouses gain value.
events.title: China closes lithium mines

events.body: The expansion of the Dostyk and Altynkol stations finishes on schedule, raising capacity from 18 to 33 trains a day. Border queues disappear, and there is more space on the Caspian ferries.
events.title: Kazakhstan doubles capacity on the Chinese border

events.body: Memory makers put customers on quotas, and electronics companies fight for components. Makers of power electronics cut production.
events.title: Memory chips go on allocation

events.body: A security incident near Bab el-Mandeb closes the southern Red Sea to merchant ships. Carriers stop sailing through Suez and send their ships around Africa.

choices.desc: Your ships that have not reached the strait sail around Africa: about 10–14 days longer and €300 per container.
choices.label: Go around the Cape

choices.desc: The carrier keeps sailing in a protected convoy. €700 per container and a small risk of damage and delay.
choices.label: Sail in a protected convoy

choices.desc: Ships wait for the strait to reopen. No surcharges, but nobody knows for how long.
choices.label: Wait in the Gulf of Aden

events.title: Red Sea closed to shipping again

events.body: Citing security, the government closes the border crossings, including the rail crossing at Małaszewicze. Trains from China are stuck on the Belarusian side.

choices.desc: New orders on the Belarus rail route will go via Suez.
choices.label: Switch the autopilot to sea

choices.desc: Trains will wait for the border to reopen.
choices.label: Stay with rail

events.title: Poland closes its border with Belarus

outcomes.body: The Commission tables its market access instrument and names batteries as a first case. Fleet buyers start asking for modules made outside China, and prices firm.
outcomes.title: Brussels proposes limits on Chinese batteries

outcomes.body: Member states cannot agree on the triggers, and the draft goes back for more work. Buyers carry on as before.
outcomes.title: The draft stalls among member states

events.title: EU market access tool takes shape

outcomes.body: The Commission proposes that firms show they do not rely on one country for critical goods. Fleet buyers start asking for battery modules and inverters from a second source.
outcomes.title: Large buyers must spread their suppliers

outcomes.body: The package sets voluntary targets and reporting only. Buyers carry on as before, and the market calms.
outcomes.title: A soft proposal with voluntary targets

events.title: Brussels proposes limits on single suppliers

label: World as of 3 Nov 2026
lead: The world starts from real news: Iran offers to reopen Hormuz within two days if its terms are met and Brent drops to $105, while on 10 November Beijing decides on export controls.

ml.why: Growth pays more than the risks cost: opening countries early wins.
